title: Feature gating decision log and customer proxy vetting for hosted tool/function-calls
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers frequently request hosted API support for customer-proxied tool/function calls (webhooks, external tools, structured outputs). These requests raise operational and security questions: when to gate a request behind a dedicated feature flag or tenancy, what vetting (network / egress controls, auth, request size/latency limits) must be completed before enabling a customer, and how to document a deterministic decision pathway for sales/CS/solutions.
goals: Create an operational decision tree that PMs and SEs can use to gate feature enablement for hosted tool/function calls
Define a minimal customer proxy vetting checklist (networking, auth, data residency, cost/rate controls, fallback strategies)
Surface required runtime and console controls to engineering (feature flags, whitelist UI, per-tenant egress policies)
Capture the decision log for compliance and for faster future onboarding
scope: Outbound tool/function call patterns for hosted API (HTTP webhook sinks, tool adapters, structured JSON outputs with tool invocation semantics)
Tenant-level gating and manual enablement flows in Console
Vetting checklist for security and infra teams
Documentation and a short training deck for Sales/CS
acceptance_criteria: A published, step-by-step decision tree (Confluence) that maps customer signals to gating outcomes (auto-allow, manual review, deny)
A one-page vetting checklist (network egress, credentials, data handling, SLO impact) signed off by Security and Infra
A Console mock (design + dev notes) showing where PM/SE can mark a tenant as allowed for toolcalls
A runbook for SEs that includes standard answers, templates for customer questionnaires, and required engineering tickets for non-trivial requests
At least two pilot onboardings completed (internal test tenants) and lessons captured
decision_log: 2025-02-20 - PM kickoff: scoped to hosted tool/function calls only; excluded private deployment-specific ops
2025-02-22 - Security (R. Gupta): add mandatory credential rotation and principle-of-least-privilege docs to checklist
2025-02-25 - Infra (M. Patel): runtime needs tenant-scoped egress controls; will prototype per-tenant egress ACLs (ENG-3910)
2025-02-27 - Product (A. Martinez): agreed on three gating buckets: auto-allow, manual-review, deny-by-policy; criteria drafted
2025-02-28 - Design (K. Rivera): Console mock completed; shows ‘Tool Integrations’ card with enablement toggle and vetting notes
tradeoffs: Auto-allow reduces friction but increases risk of noisy or expensive customer behavior — mitigated via rate limits and cost alerts
Manual review increases time-to-onboard for customers but ensures security and cost control for enterprise tenants
Building per-tenant egress controls adds engineering complexity and rollout risk; phased rollout recommended (pilot → staged rollout)
Conservative gating improves SLA predictability but can hurt PLG growth for mid-market customers
